translation_en: Abdullah bin Jafar said, I saw the Messenger of Allah eating fresh dates with cucumber. The narrators are Ibn Muqatil, Abdullah, Ibrahim bin Sad, his father, and Abdullah bin Jafar.

Anas said: My mother, Umm Sulaym, took a measure of barley, ground it, made a dish of flour and broth, and squeezed some butter from a small skin. She sent me to the Prophet while he was with his Companions and invited him. He asked, Who is with me? I returned and told her. Abu Talhah came out and said, Messenger of Allah, it is only something Umm Sulaym prepared. He entered and the food was brought. He said, Let ten people come in. They ate until full. He repeated this, admitting groups of ten until forty had eaten. Then the Prophet ate and stood up. I looked to see whether any food was missing. Anas narrated this event from his mother.
Anas was asked what he had heard the Prophet say about garlic. He replied, Whoever eats it should not come near our mosque. Anas was asked about this teaching concerning garlic.

Jabir reported that the Prophet said, Whoever eats garlic or onion should keep away from us, or keep away from our mosque. The report is from Jabir bin Abdullah through Ata and Ibn Shihab. The Prophet instructed the person who ate garlic or onions to stay away from him and the mosque.

Jabir said they were with the Messenger of Allah at Marr al-Zahran gathering fruit from the arak tree. He said, Choose the black ones, for they are the best. He was asked whether he used to tend sheep. He said, Yes; every prophet has tended them. Jabir narrated the report from Abu Salamah.

Suwayd bin al-Numan said they went with the Messenger of Allah to Khaybar. At al-Sahba he called for food, but only roasted barley flour mixed with water was brought. They ate, and he stood for prayer, rinsed his mouth, and they did the same.

Suwayd said they went with the Messenger to Khaybar. At al-Sahba, about an afternoon's journey from Khaybar, the Prophet called for food, but only roasted barley flour was brought. They chewed and ate with him. He called for water, rinsed his mouth, and they rinsed theirs. Then he led them in the sunset prayer without performing ablution. Sufyan remarked that it was as though one were hearing it from Yahya.
Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet said, When one of you has eaten, do not wipe his hand until he has licked it or had someone else lick it. Ibn Abbas narrated this instruction from the Prophet.

Jabir bin Abdullah was asked whether food cooked by fire requires ablution. He said no. In the Prophet's time they rarely found such food. When they did, they had no towels, so they wiped their hands, forearms, and feet, then prayed without performing ablution. Jabir related their practice during the Prophet's time.

Abu Umamah reported that when the Prophet's dining cloth was lifted, he would say, Abundant, wholesome, and blessed praise belongs to Allah; praise that is not repaid, not abandoned, and never dispensable, our Lord.

Abu Umamah reported that when the Prophet finished eating, or when the dining cloth was lifted, he would say, Praise belongs to Allah, who sufficed us and gave us drink; praise that is not repaid and not denied. One version says, Praise belongs to Allah, our Lord, who is not in need of us, is not abandoned, and is never dispensable, our Lord.

Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said, When one of you is served his food by his servant, if he does not seat him to eat with him, let him give him a bite or two, or a mouthful or two, for the servant has endured its heat and preparation.

Abu Masud al-Ansari said an Ansari man called Abu Shuaib had a servant who was a butcher. He saw hunger on the Prophet's face and told the servant to prepare enough food for five, so he could invite the Prophet as one of five. The servant prepared a small meal. Abu Shuaib invited the Prophet, but a man followed them. The Prophet said, Abu Shuaib, a man has followed us; if you wish, admit him, and if you wish, leave him. Abu Shuaib said, I will admit him. Abu Shuaib was one of the Ansar.

Amr bin Umayyah said he saw the Messenger of Allah cutting meat from a sheep's shoulder with a knife. He was called to prayer, so he set down the meat and knife, stood, and prayed without performing ablution. The narration is reported through al-Zuhri, from Jafar, from his father Amr bin Umayyah.
Anas reported that the Prophet said, When supper is served and the prayer is called, begin with supper. Anas bin Malik narrated this instruction from the Prophet.
Ibn Umar reported a similar statement from the Prophet. Nafi also reported that Ibn Umar once ate his supper while he could hear the imam reciting.

Aishah reported that the Prophet said, When the prayer is called and supper is ready, begin with supper. Wuhaib and Yahya bin Said reported from Hisham the wording, When supper is served. Wuhaib and Yahya bin Said also narrated this wording from Hisham.

Anas said, I am the person who knows most about the ruling of the veil; Ubayy bin Kaab used to ask me about it. The morning after the Prophet married Zainab bint Jahsh in Medina, he invited people to a meal after the day had grown bright. The people left, but some men stayed sitting with him. The Prophet got up and walked, and I walked with him as far as Aishah's room. He thought they had left, so I returned with him, but they were still sitting there. He turned back, and I went with him again as far as Aishah's door. He returned, and I returned with him. This time they had stood up. He then placed a screen between me and himself, and the verse of the veil was revealed.

Abu Musa said a boy was born to him, so he brought him to the Prophet. The Prophet named him Ibrahim, rubbed a chewed date on his palate, prayed for his blessing, and returned him to Abu Musa. He was Abu Musa's eldest son.
A child was brought to the Prophet so that he could perform tahnik for him, and the child urinated on him. The Prophet then poured water over the place.

Asma bint Abi Bakr said she was pregnant with Abdullah bin al-Zubair in Mecca. When her pregnancy was full term, she set out and reached Medina, stopping at Quba, where she gave birth. She brought the baby to the Messenger of Allah, placed him in his lap, and he asked for a date. He chewed it, then put some of his saliva into the child's mouth. The first thing to enter the child's stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah. He rubbed the date on the baby's palate, prayed for him, and blessed him. Abdullah was the first child born in Islam, and the Muslims rejoiced greatly because they had been told that the Jews had bewitched them so that no children would be born to them.

Anas said Abu Talhah's son was ill. Abu Talhah went out, and the child died. When Abu Talhah returned, he asked about his son. Umm Sulaym said he was more peaceful than he had been. She brought him supper, and he ate. Then he was intimate with her. Afterward she told him to bury the child. In the morning Abu Talhah went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. The Prophet asked, Did you spend the night as newlyweds? Abu Talhah said yes. The Prophet prayed, O Allah, bless them both. She gave birth to a boy. Abu Talhah told Anas to take him to the Prophet. He was brought with some dates. The Prophet asked whether he had anything with him. They said yes, dates. He took one, chewed it, took it from his mouth, put it into the baby's mouth, rubbed it on his palate, and named him Abdullah.
Muhammad bin al-Muthanna narrated this report from Ibn Abi Adi, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad, from Anas, then transmitted the same account.

Salman bin Amir reported the saying, With a boy there is an aqiqah sacrifice. Hajjaj reported it through Hammad, from Ayyub, Qatadah, Hisham, and Habib, from Ibn Sirin, from Salman, from the Prophet. Other narrators reported it from Asim and Hisham, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from al-Rabab, from Salman, from the Prophet. Yazid bin Ibrahim reported it from Ibn Sirin from Salman as his own statement.

Salman bin Amir al-Dabbi said he heard the Messenger of Allah say, With a boy there is an aqiqah sacrifice, so shed blood on his behalf and remove the harm from him. Abdullah bin Abi al-Aswad also reported that Ibn Sirin asked al-Hasan who had told him the hadith about aqiqah. Al-Hasan said he heard it from Samurah bin Jundub. The report also records how al-Hasan identified Samurah bin Jundub as his source.

Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said, There is no fara and no atirah. Fara was the first offspring of an animal, which people used to sacrifice to their idols; atirah was a sacrifice offered in Rajab.

Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said, There is no fara and no atirah. Fara was the first offspring born to them, which they sacrificed to their idols, and atirah was an offering in Rajab. The first offspring was sacrificed to their idols, and the Rajab sacrifice was called atirah.

Adi bin Hatim asked the Prophet about hunting with a mihraz, a blunt-sided hunting stick. He said, Eat what it strikes with its sharp edge, but what it strikes with its broad side is a beaten animal. Adi also asked about hunting with a dog. The Prophet said, Eat what your dog catches for you, for its capture is like slaughter. If you find another dog with your dog and fear it helped catch and kill the prey, do not eat it, because you said Allah's name over your dog and not over the other.

Adi bin Hatim asked about hunting with a mihraz. The Prophet said, If you strike with its sharp edge, eat; if it hits with its broad side and kills, it is a beaten animal, so do not eat. Adi said he released his dog. The Prophet said, If you release your dog after naming Allah, eat. Adi asked what if the dog eats from the prey. The Prophet said not to eat, because the dog did not hold it for you but for itself. Adi asked about finding another dog with his. The Prophet said not to eat, because you named Allah over your own dog and not over the other.

Adi bin Hatim said, Messenger of Allah, we send out trained dogs. The Prophet said, Eat what they catch for you. Adi asked, Even if they kill it? He said, Even if they kill it. Adi asked about hunting with a mihraz. The Prophet said, Eat what it pierces with its sharp edge, but do not eat what it strikes with its broad side.
